title: Los Angeles weather: Storm expected to bring heavy rain, flood risk to Southern California. Here's the timeline - ABC7 Los Angeles
text:
Los Angeles weather: Storm expected to bring heavy rain, flood risk to Southern California. Here's the timeline - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California Weather 
 Storm bringing rain, possible flooding to SoCal. Here's how long wet conditions will last 
 Thursday, November 19, 2026 4:36PM 
 Este artículo se ofrece en Español A powerful storm moving through Southern California is expected to drench the region and bring heavy rain, strong winds and possible flooding. KABC LOS ANGELES (KABC) -- A powerful storm moving through Southern California is expected to drench the region and bring heavy rain, strong winds and possible flooding on Thursday.
 The timing of the storm is expected to create a messy morning commute.
 Widespread but light showers are moving into Ventura County and parts of Los Angeles County, but it's expected to get heavier as the morning progresses. Widespread rain is expected during the morning rush hour, impacting drivers on the road.
 A flood watch will remain in effect for Ventura County and much of Los Angeles County through Thursday afternoon.
 Thunderstorms are possible during periods of heavier rain, bringing a threat of downpours, gusty winds and lightning.
 The storm is expected to move out relatively quickly, with conditions beginning to clear out starting Thursday afternoon. However, showers could linger into Friday.
 A high surf advisory is in effect for beaches in Ventura and Los Angeles counties through Friday morning, while the Orange County coast is under a beach hazards statement through Friday morning.
 Thursday forecast
 Los Angeles and Orange counties Thursday can expect rainfall totals between 1 and 2 inches, along with a high of 64 and a low of 47.
 The valleys and Inland Empire Thursday will see a high of 65 degrees and a low of 43. Rainfall totals between 1 and 3 inches are possible.
 Beach communities Thursday can expect a high of 70 and a low of 53. The storm could bring between 1 to 2 inches of rain.
 Mountain communities will be partly cloudy Thursday, with a high of 43 degrees and a chilly overnight low of 23. Rainfall totals of 2 to 4 inches are possible Thursday, with snow falling at elevations above 7,500 feet.
 Desert areas can expect a high of 58 and a low of 31 Thursday, with Palm Springs reaching a high of 71. Up to 1 inch of rain is possible.
 City News Service contributed to this report.
